system_note: Reviewed billed diagnoses and procedures against the medical record for Claim MR_07. Supported by the record: massive bilateral pulmonary embolism with right heart strain and catheter-directed thrombolysis (I26.09) (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 474; Procedure Note - CT Pulmonary Angiography, p. 193); pre-hospital cardiac arrest with ROSC and emergency defibrillation/intubation supporting I46.9 and the airway/CPR procedure codes (Emergency Department Provider Note, p. 474); acute respiratory failure with hypoxia on ABG and mechanical ventilation (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 474; Critical Care Progress Note, p. 162). Right-sided DVT documented on duplex supports I82.401 with POA = N (Physical & Occupational Therapy Consultation, p. 56). Severe sepsis / septic shock (R65.21) is documented during the ICU course with very high procalcitonin, lactate and antibiotics for presumed blood infection (Critical Care Progress Note, p. 162; Patient & Family Education, pp. 18-830). Not supported / unsupported as billed: two billed MCC diagnosis lines lack adequate clinical documentation in the chart to justify the specific ICD-10 descriptors submitted. (1) I50.30 Unspecified diastolic (congestive) heart failure - the record documents acute right ventricular failure/strain from massive PE and explicitly states preserved left ventricular ejection fraction on echo; there is no documentation of diastolic (left-sided) congestive heart failure (Echocardiogram, p. 17; History & Physical (Admitting), p. 474). (2) G93.1 Anoxic brain damage - neurology and the discharge summary describe an encouraging neurologic exam and "excellent neurologic recovery," and the problem list documents post-arrest cognitive dysfunction which resolved; there is no contemporaneous documentation of anoxic brain injury meeting the usual threshold for G93.1 (Neurology Consultation, p. 604; Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 833-834). Because these two codes are billed as MCCs but lack support as coded, they must be removed (or recoded only if explicit physician documentation of anoxic brain injury or diastolic heart failure is added). Procedure discrepancy: 5A1D80Z (Performance of urinary filtration, prolonged intermittent, <6 hrs/day) is billed but the admission H&P and problem list state the AKI was managed conservatively and specifically note "non-dialysis, recovered," with no procedure note documenting hemodialysis/ultrafiltration/CRRT in the chart passages retrieved; therefore 5A1D80Z is not supported (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 474). Other interventional procedures (catheter-directed thrombolysis, IVC filter insertion, intubation, central line/arterial line placement, restoration of cardiac rhythm) are supported by procedure/clinical notes (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 474; Procedure Note - CT Pulmonary Angiography, p. 193; Emergency Department Provider Note, p. 474). Correction applied: remove unsupported diagnoses G93.1 and I50.30 from the claim, and remove unsupported procedure 5A1D80Z. Principal diagnosis remains I26.09 (massive PE with acute cor pulmonale) per admission H&P and imaging. POA flags left as documented for codes retained (e.g., I82.401 POA = N supported by duplex documentation occurring after admission). See evidence citations below for the exact supporting/contradicting text used to make these determinations.
rationale_letter: Re: Claim MR_07 - Audit Determination We completed a medical record audit of the above-referenced inpatient stay (admit 03/13/2026) to determine whether the submitted diagnosis and procedure codes are supported by the documented clinical record. Based on the documentation we found the following: Finding: Two billed diagnoses and one billed procedure are not supported as submitted. Basis for Finding (record evidence relied upon): - I26.09 (Other pulmonary embolism with acute cor pulmonale) - supported. CT pulmonary angiography and angiography notes document a massive bilateral saddle pulmonary embolism with right-heart strain, and the admitting H&P documents catheter-directed thrombolysis performed (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 474; Procedure Note - CT Pulmonary Angiography, p. 193). - I46.9 (Cardiac arrest) and related resuscitation/airway procedures - supported by EMS/ED notes documenting pulseless ventricular tachycardia, CPR with ROSC after 15 minutes, multiple defibrillations, and emergent intubation (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 474; Emergency Department Provider Note, p. 474). - J96.01 (Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia), N17.9 (AKI), I82.401 (right lower extremity DVT), and R65.21 (severe sepsis/septic shock) - supported by ABG values, rising creatinine with problem-list AKI (non-dialysis), documented duplex ultrasound showing right femoral/popliteal DVT, high procalcitonin/lactate and use of broad-spectrum antibiotics for bloodstream infection (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 474; Critical Care Progress Note, p. 162; Physical & Occupational Therapy Consultation, p. 56; Patient & Family Education, pp. 18-830). Unsupported items and correction applied: 1) I50.30 - Unspecified diastolic (congestive) heart failure: NOT SUPPORTED. The echocardiogram documents right ventricular dilation and severe hypokinesis with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction and the record describes acute right heart failure/strain related to PE rather than left-sided diastolic congestive heart failure (Echocardiogram, p. 17; History & Physical (Admitting), p. 474). We are removing I50.30 from the claim. 2) G93.1 - Anoxic brain damage: NOT SUPPORTED as coded. Neurology documentation and the discharge summary document an encouraging neurologic exam and "excellent neurologic recovery" after targeted temperature management; there is no contemporaneous documentation of anoxic brain injury meeting the typical clinical threshold required to assign G93.1 (Neurology Consultation, p. 604; Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 833-834). We are removing G93.1 from the claim. 3) Procedure 5A1D80Z - Performance of urinary filtration, prolonged intermittent, <6 hrs/day: NOT SUPPORTED. The admission H&P and active problem list explicitly note AKI was "non-dialysis, recovered" and there is no procedural documentation retrieved showing hemodialysis/ultrafiltration or CRRT was performed (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 474). We are removing 5A1D80Z from the procedure roster. Corrective action taken: The claim should be adjusted to remove I50.30 and G93.1 from the diagnosis list and to remove procedure 5A1D80Z from the procedure list. The principal diagnosis remains I26.09 (Other pulmonary embolism with acute cor pulmonale), which is supported by imaging and procedure notes. Remaining diagnoses and procedures retained on audit are supported in the chart as cited. If you disagree with these adjustments, please provide the specific physician documentation you rely upon that supports the clinical criteria for (a) diastolic heart failure (I50.30) and/or (b) anoxic brain damage (G93.1), and/or (c) an explicit dialysis/ultrafiltration procedure note for the billed urinary filtration code. Absent such documentation, the audit determination and recommended removals will stand. Sincerely, Senior Clinical Claims Auditor (Record citations and excerpts provided in the enclosed evidence list.)

evidence_cited.excerpt: CT pulmonary angiography confirmed massive bilateral saddle pulmonary embolism with right heart strain. Given hemodynamic instability, catheter-directed thrombolysis was performed with tissue plasminogen activator.

evidence_cited.citation: Procedure Note - CT Pulmonary Angiography, p. 193
evidence_cited.excerpt: Bilateral massive pulmonary artery emboli with saddle embolus at the main pulmonary artery bifurcation. Extensive clot burden in bilateral pulmonary arteries with occlusion of segmental branches. Right heart strain with dilation and hypokinesis.
Right ventricular dilation with severe hypokinesis. Left ventricular ejection fraction preserved. No pericardial effusion. Findings consistent with acute right heart strain from massive PE.

Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after 15 minutes of CPR with three defibrillation attempts and multiple rounds of ACLS medications. On arrival to the emergency department the patient was intubated with GCS 3 pre-sedation.
Post-arrest patient with encouraging early neurologic exam. Neuroprognostication at 72 hours indicated intact function with follow-up expected excellent.

Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses Resolved massive pulmonary embolism status post catheter-directed thrombolysis; resolved cardiac arrest with successful ROSC; excellent neurologic recovery post-arrest; resolved right ventricular dysfunction; resolved AKI; right common femoral DVT on anticoagulation; IVC filter in place; hypothyroidism; depression; ICU-acquired weakness.
